references.text: The Lord's right hand is described as exalted and as the one who performs mighty deeds, the same theme concerning the power and victory of God's right hand.
God's arm is described as strong and His right hand as exalted, parallel to the description of the Lord's right hand as glorious in power.
The Lord's right hand and holy arm have given Him victory, the same motif of God's right hand bringing salvation and victory over enemies.
A prayer that God would save with His right hand refers to God's right hand as an instrument of deliverance.
God's glorious arm that led the people through the water refers back to the Exodus from Egypt and God's mighty deeds.
At the Lord's right hand there was flaming fire, describing God's majesty and power.
The Lord's right hand won the land for Israel by driving out the enemies, the same theme of God crushing foes.
Christ is exalted at God's right hand, a New Testament fulfillment of the motif of God's right hand as a symbol of power and honor.
Both verses confirm that the Lord's right hand is the direct instrument of God's victorious, miraculous deeds.
Both verses share the specific motif that the Lord's power must 'crush' the enemy's ability to rise up against His people.
The motif of the Lord's hand crushing enemies expands from a historical victory to a prophetic judgment over kingdoms.
The Lord's right hand is consistently portrayed as the instrument of deliverance that intervenes against the enemy's wrath.
Both verses link the Lord's right hand to the demonstration of awe-inspiring and glorious deeds toward enemies.
Both verses highlight the Lord's hand as an active tool for finding and striking those who hate His people.
